a_raw: {"translation":"Target is the proposition that for every arithmetic theory F, given a Δ₁ presentation of its axiom set and the hypothesis that every theorem of IΣ₁ is a theorem of F, F proves the single implication “if F's standard provability predicate does not hold of the code of falsehood, then γ,” where γ is the Gödel sentence for that predicate: IΣ₁ proves that γ is equivalent to the assertion that the predicate does not hold of the code of γ. The implication is inside arithmetic. No consistency or soundness of F is assumed, and F is not required to prove the antecedent or the consequent separately."}
translation: Target is the proposition that for every arithmetic theory F, given a Δ₁ presentation of its axiom set and the hypothesis that every theorem of IΣ₁ is a theorem of F, F proves the single implication “if F's standard provability predicate does not hold of the code of falsehood, then γ,” where γ is the Gödel sentence for that predicate: IΣ₁ proves that γ is equivalent to the assertion that the predicate does not hold of the code of γ. The implication is inside arithmetic. No consistency or soundness of F is assumed, and F is not required to prove the antecedent or the consequent separately.

divergences.description: Chalmers considers a sound F. The target does not assume soundness, so it strengthens item (b) to cover unsound theories as well. Soundness is not needed to prove the conditional.
The target fixes a specific setting that the passage leaves implicit: F is an arithmetic theory with a Δ₁ axiom presentation that proves every theorem of IΣ₁.
The consequent is G(F) itself, rather than a separate assertion of its truth. This is the usual disquotational reading of “G(F) is true” for this particular sentence.

judgement.summary: The target gets the scope of item (b) right: F proves the whole conditional, with its own consistency as antecedent and its own Gödel sentence as consequent. It does not say that F proves either one separately.
